reason: At unlock, sklearn 1.9's pandas ARFF parser raised TypeError under pandas 3 on integer-like nominal levels (WDBC Class {1,2}). Added a fallback to sklearn's LIAC-ARFF parser for the same md5-verified file. Parsing only; no change to method, data, splits or metrics. Dev datasets still parse with the pandas parser and match their pinned sha256.
test_heldout_not_present_on_disk encodes a pre-unlock invariant that becomes false by design once held-out data are fetched; it now skips when PREREGISTRATION.md is locked.

Found while checking the first two complete seeds (held-out results visible): every deployed MO-Fuzzy and SO-GA-Fuzzy(hybrid) model on Thyroid (15/15 each) had diverged consequents (intercept ~ -1e12, constant test predictions, AUROC 0.5), although their inner-CV objectives were good. Cause: fit_logistic_l2 used plain Newton steps, which overshoot on imbalanced data with a rule that fires on a small high-risk subgroup and then explode on saturated logits. Fix: backtracking (step-halving) on the exact penalised objective; full steps that do not increase it are accepted unchanged, so the estimator and the method are unchanged, only the numerical solver is made convergent (verified equal to sklearn's LogisticRegression to 1e-4). Consequences: (i) all 300 MO-Fuzzy and SO-GA-Fuzzy(hybrid) fits (both use the solver during search and refit) are re-run with the fixed code; the 174 superseded checkpoints are archived in results/final/superseded_D3/ and summarised in results/final/superseded_D3_records.csv; (ii) the same solver computes the calibration slope/intercept of every model, so scripts/analyze.py recomputes all outcome metrics from the stored test-fold predictions with the fixed code (changes reported in stats.json); predictions of all other models are unaffected. No change to the design, hyperparameters, data, splits, hypotheses or analysis plan.
New regression test for D3 (synthetic design that makes plain Newton diverge; solver must match sklearn).
